style.name: Conveyor Factory
style.description: A bright, friendly modern packing line at three-quarter height: cream floor with painted safety lines, mint-green and safety-yellow machinery with rounded guards, black ribbed belts on steel frames, kraft cartons, coloured totes and poly parcels, overhead signboards, red/amber/green stack lights, a yellow robot arm and soft skylight daylight. A process becomes a production line: items enter at a planned rate and every item's position is a closed-form function of time through belt segments; stations transform them as they pass (scanner tags, diverter sorts, press stamps, filler loads, quality gate rejects one down a chute, wrapper seals, robot arm picks and places), queues build where a station is slower than the belt, stack lights follow station state and overhead counters tick.
motion: Items enter from the hood up an incline belt at a planned release rate; every item's position is a closed-form function of (t - release) along its route, with holds at stations.
Accumulation: an item never comes closer than one pitch to the item ahead on the same belt, so a slow station grows a visible queue that advances in steps when the head leaves.

Stations transform items as they pass: the scanner curtain sweeps and a tag appears; the diverter arm swings totes onto the curved lane; the press ram stamps a mark; the filler pours a tote to a level.
The quality gate flags one item, the pusher shoves it onto the roller chute where it slides into the bin (red light); the wrapper ring spins and items leave sealed in film.

The robot arm (analytic two-joint IK) picks each item at the end stop and places it on the pallet grid; belts scroll and rollers turn at belt speed; stack lights and overhead counters follow the plan.

objects.procedural: cream painted concrete floor (yellow walkway lines, hatched robot / reject zones), pale back wall with high windows and steel columns

notes.data: SAMPLE DATA: the counters (scanned / filled / rejected / packed) are counts of planned events, not measurements.
notes.mechanism: line.js plans every item through the belt network as a pure function of time: free-flow knots from a FIFO discrete-event pass over the release schedule, then per-frame accumulation (an item never closer than one pitch to the one ahead). The filler (2.0 s dwell) is slower than the tote burst, so a queue grows on the curved lane.
notes.framing: own window check ok (worst over -0.0196 at 14.8s); kit safe ok (worst 0.8904)
